items.text: This checklist is not an authoritative document. Full reference must be made to the individual aircraft flight Manual/Pilot Operating handbook as amended. Current ANO and AICs and Pilot Order book/Flying School Syllabus, local procedures, may also be relevant.
Aircraft Documents — Documentation complete and satisfactory, including valid Certificate of Maintenance if required.
Weather — Local, en-route and destination forecasts and actuals.
Flight Planning — Current AIP/Flight Guide, NOTAMS, Amendments and bulletins. PPR, Daylight remaining, etc.
Fuel — Sufficient to destination and alternates, Contingency.
Charts — Current and sufficient coverage for flight.
Weight & Balance — Load (passengers, baggage, fuel) within limits.
Performance — Take-off, en-route and range, landing.
Passengers — Comfort and safety briefing, emergency procedures.
Pilot — Licence and experience current and valid. Medical certificate valid, fitness for flight.
Survival Equipment — For over water flight - dinghy accessible, lifejackets worn but not inflated, Flares, Transceiver, ELT.
Book-Out — Departure ATC, airfield movements book, aircraft tech. log.
Flight Plan — File for IFR and International Flights, flight across water and sparsely populated areas.

sections.title: Pre-Flight Action Of Pilot In Command — Approaching Aircraft

items.text: Check — Access to taxiways, obstructions, level surface, for fuel / oil spillages.
Remove — ANY ice or frost from ALL aircraft surfaces.

items.text: If taxying, stop clear of other aircraft, fuel trucks/stations, etc.
Evacuate to a safe distance upwind, taking fire extinguisher.
Forced landing procedure or diversion as applicable.

items.response: CHECK FREQUENCY, VOLUME, SQUELCH, CHECK AVIONICS SELECTOR/SWITCHES
CHECK PLUGS SECURE, CHANGE HEADSETS, TRY HAND MICROPHONE
CHECK AMMETER, MASTER SWITCH, CIRCUIT BREAKERS - RESET ONCE ONLY

items.text: Speechless / Transmit blind / Non-radio procedure as appropriate.
If NO OUTPUT — Reset Master Switch (off for 2 secs, then on)
items.response: IF OUTPUT RESTORED — RESTORE ESSENTIAL ELECTRICS SINGLY

items.text: IN THE EVENT OF REPEATED/CONTINUED ELECTRICAL FAILURE: select only essential electrical services, divert if applicable, note radio transmission makes a particularly heavy drain on the battery.
Lower nose to maintain best glide airspeed.
Brief passengers/tighten harness/unlatch door as time permits.

sections.title: Engine Failure At Altitude (Forced Landing Without Power)

items.text: Attain and maintain best glide speed – TRIM.

items.response: CHANGE TANKS, CHECK SUFFICIENT, FUEL PUMP ON

items.text: If engine does not restart, R/T MAYDAY call, committed checks

sections.title: Ditching At Sea — Ditching Procedure (Without Power)

items.text: Establish glide, head for coast line or any shipping area, check for causes of failure as time permits.
Large swell / Light wind : land along swell, tail down stalled. Light swell / Strong wind : Landing into wind, tail down stalled.
DO NOT INFLATE LIFE JACKETS IN CABIN
Emergencies by their nature are not standard, and this checklist can only provide a guide to the appropriate actions - in an emergency: PILOT JUDGEMENT SHOULD DICTATE PILOT ACTIONS.
